title: 'I'm Generally Not Keen on Sequels': Why Rajinikanth Rejected Baasha 2 and Petta 2
excerpt: The superstar explained why he said no to revisiting his classics but yes to Jailer 2 — and revealed the sequel's missing ingredient: a song with Tamannaah.
body:
• Rajinikanth has confirmed he turned down sequel pitches for his classics Baasha and Petta — Petta 2 was to be directed by Karthik Subbaraj — saying he is "generally not keen on sequels."
  • The superstar made an exception for Jailer 2 because, in his words, the first film "had the right setup for a sequel." He also revealed the sequel was missing one element: "a song with Tamannaah."
  • Director Nelson Dilipkumar was initially sceptical about the sequel himself, and postponed a Telugu film to make it happen.
  • Jailer 2 releases October 15, 2026, with Sun Pictures confirming the date after speculation about reshoots pushing it back.

No to Baasha 2, no to Petta 2

In a career spanning nearly five decades, Rajinikanth has almost never done a sequel. Now he has explained why. The superstar confirmed that he rejected pitches for Baasha 2 and Petta 2 — the latter with Karthik Subbaraj, who directed the 2019 original — telling interviewers he is "generally not keen on sequels" and doesn't prefer them.

It is not the first time the classics have been approached. Director Vashishta Mallidi, who wrote a Baasha sequel script under the Dil Raju banner and received a positive response from Rajinikanth, ultimately shelved the project himself, saying the story didn't feel right. Earlier pitches were rejected for a simpler reason: neither Rajinikanth nor director Suresh Krissna wanted to touch the legacy of the 1995 film that made him a mass icon.

"I'm generally not keen on sequels."

— Rajinikanth, on rejecting Baasha 2 and Petta 2
https://youtube.com/watch?v=yBT-KF3oiwA

Why Jailer got the exception

The one sequel Rajinikanth did agree to was Jailer 2, reuniting him with director Nelson Dilipkumar. His reasoning: the 2023 original, in which he played the retired jailer Muthuvel "Tiger" Pandian, had the right setup for a continuation — the ending left a syndicate in play and brought together Rajinikanth, Shivarajkumar, and Mohanlal for a multi-front climax that practically demanded a follow-up.

https://x.com/CinemaXverse/status/2108546717851570448

Even the director hesitated. Nelson was initially sceptical about making a sequel and postponed a Telugu project to commit to it. Rajinikanth also revealed that the film was missing what he considered an essential element: "a song with Tamannaah" — a nod to the viral "Kaavaalaa" number from the first film that became a cultural phenomenon.

The film itself

Jailer 2 arrives October 15, 2026, with Sun Pictures confirming the date after speculation that reshoots might delay it. The sequel brings back Ramya Krishnan, Mohanlal, Shivarajkumar, Mirnaa Menon, Yogi Babu, and Jaffer Saadiq, with new additions including Suraj Venjaramoodu, Bagavathi Perumal, and Mithun Chakraborty. Vijay Sethupathi joined the cast in a cameo role after reports that Nandamuri Balakrishna passed due to busy commitments.

The original Jailer was one of the biggest Tamil hits of 2023, and the sequel — announced in January 2025, shot through this year, wrapped in April — is the most consequential release of Rajinikanth's recent run. At 75, the superstar's choice of projects now carries the weight of legacy: what he makes, and what he refuses to remake.

Diaspora angle

Baasha remains the film that made Rajinikanth a household name for the Tamil diaspora — from the 1995 original's fans in Singapore and Malaysia to the Japanese audience that discovered him through Muthu. The news that Baasha 2 will never happen closes a decades-long rumor cycle, while Jailer 2's global release gives overseas fans the sequel the actor himself chose to make.

What to watch

All eyes are on October 15: whether Jailer 2 justifies the one exception Rajinikanth has made in 50 years, and how the box office responds to a sequel whose own star once doubted the form. Beyond that, the actor has said he will take a short break after Jailer 2 before deciding his next move.
